concepts.label: vpn-service
concepts.gloss: A vpn-service is the provider-managed Layer 3 VPN service as a whole, spanning all participating sites and realized by VPN-specific instances on one or more provider-edge network elements.
concepts.example: ACME-L3VPN connects CE-A, CE-B, and CE-C through VPN nodes on PE1, PE2, and PE3, with CE-A acting as the hub site and the other two sites as spokes.

concepts.label: vpn-node
concepts.gloss: A vpn-node is the per-network-element realization of part of a Layer 3 VPN service, hosting that service's local access attachments, routing state, identifiers, and policies on a particular provider device.
concepts.example: vpn-node@PE1 is ACME-L3VPN's local VPN instance on PE1 and contains the access toward CE-A, RD 65000:101, and the applicable route-target and routing policies.

concepts.label: vpn-network-access
concepts.gloss: A vpn-network-access is the service attachment on a VPN node through which that node connects to and exchanges customer traffic and routes with a particular customer-edge peer.
concepts.example: access-PE2-CEB is the attachment on vpn-node@PE2 facing CE-B, using the 10.0.2.0/30 connection, OSPF, and the silver-50M QoS profile.

concepts.label: ce
concepts.gloss: A ce is the customer-edge routing peer reached by a VPN network access and paired with a provider-edge network element at the customer–provider boundary.
concepts.example: CE-A peers with PE1 over access-PE1-CEA and supplies the hub site's customer routes to ACME-L3VPN.

concepts.label: route-distinguisher
concepts.gloss: A route-distinguisher is the identifier assigned to a VPN node's routing context to make otherwise overlapping customer IPv4 or IPv6 prefixes globally distinct as VPN routes.
concepts.example: On vpn-node@PE1, RD 65000:101 turns customer prefix 192.0.2.0/24 into the distinct VPN route identified by 65000:101:192.0.2.0/24.

concepts.label: vpn-target
concepts.gloss: A vpn-target is a route-target policy value associated with VPN routes to control which VPN nodes export those routes and which VPN nodes import them, thereby determining service connectivity.
concepts.example: In ACME-L3VPN, routes from the hub can be marked with RT 65000:2 for import by spoke VPN nodes, while spoke routes can be marked with RT 65000:1 for import by the hub VPN node.

concepts.label: ip-connection
concepts.gloss: An ip-connection is the IP addressing configuration of a VPN network access, including the subnet or endpoint addresses used for communication between the provider edge and customer edge.
concepts.example: For access-PE1-CEA, subnet 10.0.1.0/30 can assign 10.0.1.1 to PE1 and 10.0.1.2 to CE-A.

concepts.label: qos-profile
concepts.gloss: A qos-profile is the traffic-treatment and capacity policy applied to a VPN network access, such as bandwidth limits, classification, scheduling, or priority behavior.
concepts.example: Applying gold-200M to access-PE1-CEA gives that attachment the provider-defined gold traffic treatment with a 200-Mbit/s service rate.

concepts.label: ne
concepts.gloss: An ne is a provider network element that acts as a provider edge by hosting one or more per-service VPN nodes and terminating accesses toward customer-edge peers.
concepts.example: PE2 hosts vpn-node@PE2 for ACME-L3VPN and terminates access-PE2-CEB toward CE-B.

concepts.label: routing-protocol
concepts.gloss: A routing-protocol is the dynamic or static route-exchange method configured on a VPN network access between its provider-edge VPN context and the facing customer edge.
concepts.example: OSPF PE2-CEB runs on access-PE2-CEB so that PE2 and CE-B can advertise and learn the site's IP prefixes.

concepts.label: routing-policy
concepts.gloss: A routing-policy is a set of route-selection or transformation rules applied at a VPN node when importing routes into, or exporting routes from, its VPN routing context.
concepts.example: ACME-export-policy on vpn-node@PE1 permits CE-A's approved prefixes, attaches the hub's designated route target, and rejects all other customer routes.

concepts.label: sla-report
concepts.gloss: An sla-report is an assurance record for a VPN service that summarizes measured service-level performance and compliance over a reporting period.
concepts.example: The ACME monthly SLA report records ACME-L3VPN's availability, latency, loss, and any SLA breaches for August 2026.

concepts.label: x-op-tag-91
concepts.gloss: x-op-tag-91 is an operator- or vendor-specific opaque attribute carried on a VPN node whose semantics are not defined by the standard L3NM model and must be interpreted by the proprietary extension owner.
concepts.example: vpn-node@PE1 carries x-op-tag-91=A7, which the operator's implementation can process according to its private meaning without the standard model assigning semantics to A7.
